thread.title: Real Madrid agree record £115m deal for Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig
thread.title_full: Real Madrid agree record £115m deal for Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig

author: Liam O'Connor Sports Editor
title: Real Madrid agree record £115m deal for Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig
text:
Real Madrid agreed a club-record fee of €135m (£115.7m) with RB Leipzig on Wednesday to sign 19-year-old winger Yan Diomande. The deal, which makes Diomande the most expensive African player in history, coincides with Madrid’s efforts to secure a contract extension for Brazil forward Vinícius Júnior amid interest from Arsenal.
The agreement for Diomande follows several weeks of negotiations that saw Paris Saint-Germain withdraw from the pursuit.
Yan Diomande’s Record-Breaking Transfer
The total package of €135m eclipses the fee Real Madrid paid Borussia Dortmund in 2023 for Jude Bellingham, which was believed to be worth up to €134m including add-ons. Diomande, who starred for Côte d’Ivoire at the World Cup, is expected to sign a contract that runs until 2031.
This move sets a new financial benchmark for African talent. The fee surpasses the £72m Arsenal spent on Nicolas Pépé in 2019, establishing Diomande as the most expensive African player in football history. The teenager’s rise has been rapid; after joining RB Leipzig from Leganés last summer, he was pictured arriving at the German side’s pre-season training camp in Austria on Wednesday.
The transfer also triggers a financial windfall for his former club. Leganés are due a 5% sell-on fee from the transaction. The player had made only 10 first-team appearances for Leganés before they sold him to Leipzig for €20m (£17.4m).
Contract Negotiations with Vinícius Júnior
While Madrid celebrates a new arrival, they are simultaneously fighting to keep a cornerstone of their attack. Vinícius Júnior, 26, has less than a year remaining on his contract, leaving the club vulnerable to poaching. On Wednesday, the Brazilian and his representatives at Roc Nation held talks with Madrid officials regarding an extension.
Despite some reports that Vinícius had rejected previous offers, sources in Spain describe recent talks as positive. The player is reportedly weighing an improved deal closer to the €30m per season he requested.
Vinícius shared those words on Tuesday, noting that Madrid’s new manager, José Mourinho, wants him to maintain that mindset after his return to pre-season training following the World Cup.
Arsenal’s Aggressive Attack Overhaul
The tug-of-war over Vinícius is part of a broader, aggressive recruitment drive by Mikel Arteta’s Arsenal. The North London club has already agreed to a £75m deal to sign Bruno Guimarães from Newcastle, a teammate of Vinícius on the Brazilian national team.
Arsenal’s search for attacking reinforcements has been marked by several high-profile targets and missed opportunities. The club missed out on England forward Morgan Rogers last month, who joined Chelsea for a British record fee of £117m. Currently, Arsenal is exploring other options should Vinícius renew with Madrid, including PSG’s Bradley Barcola, who is valued at approximately £145m and also sought by Liverpool.
Additionally, Arsenal is hoping to persuade 26-year-old Julián Alvarez to join them, even as Barcelona’s sporting director, Deco, held talks with Atlético Madrid on Wednesday to secure the Argentina forward.
Madrid’s Strategic Squad Composition
The acquisition of Diomande is not a replacement for Vinícius, but rather an expansion of Madrid’s arsenal.
This move aligns with a long-term strategy of investing in elite teenage talent—a pattern previously seen with the development of players like Rodrygo and Vinícius himself. By pairing world-class established stars with record-breaking young prospects, Madrid is attempting to insulate its dominance in European football against the aging of its current core.
Market Movement and Pending Decisions
The immediate focus now shifts to the finalization of Diomande’s contract and the resolution of the Vinícius stalemate. With the transfer window active, the decision of the Brazilian forward to either accept the €30m-per-season offer or move to the Premier League will dictate whether Arsenal pivots toward targets like Bradley Barcola or Julián Alvarez.
